AlternateTargets: why did the Patriarch come from the West?

what is the meaning of Bodhidharma's coming from the West?

Senses.Explanation: What is the meaning of the Patriarch's coming from the West? The Patriarch is Bodhidharma, and the west is India in relation to China. This is a very frequent stock question in lamp records and recorded sayings: the full form occurs 1,858 times in 231 allowlisted texts, while the shorter noun phrase “the meaning of the Patriarch's coming from the West” (祖師西來意) occurs 2,081 times. The records preserve different replies by named people. Zhaozhou Congshen answers “the cypress tree in the garden” (庭前柏樹子). Linji Yixuan, asked while washing his feet, answers “just now this old monk is washing his feet” (恰值老僧洗脚). National Teacher Huian answers Tannan and Nanyue Huairang, “why not ask about your own meaning?” (何不問自己意). Mazu Daoyi tells Letan Fahui, “lower your voice; come closer” (低聲，近前來), and then strikes him. Jingshan Daoqin answers an unnamed monk, “your question is improper” (汝問不當). Damei Fachang answers, “there was no meaning in the coming from the West” (西來無意). Lingyin Huiyuan later reports that Wuzu Fayan placed Zhaozhou's question and cypress answer beside “What is Buddha?” and Dongshan Shouchu's “three catties of hemp” (如何是佛，麻三斤) immediately before Yuanwu Keqin's awakening. The question therefore remains one stable public-interview prompt even though its recorded answers differ; the entry does not turn those answers into paraphrases of one hidden proposition.
Senses.Note: A stock question spoken in public exchanges, not a private idiom. Each AttributionNote identifies the questioner and respondent; an actor remains unnamed only after the six-rung attribution review. Compare the shorter noun phrase “the meaning of the Patriarch's coming from the West” (祖師西來意).

Occurrences.Kwic: 然則如何是祖師西來意。師云。庭前柏樹子。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Book of Serenity (萬松老人評唱天童覺和尚頌古從容庵錄), Zhaozhou's cypress case. An unnamed monk is the exact questioner who again asks the meaning of the ancestral teacher's coming from the west after objecting to presentation by an object; Zhaozhou Congshen answers 'the cypress tree before the hall.' The line, expanded context, section header, book title, TEI header, and parallel versions do not name the monk.

Occurrences.Kwic: 有僧坦然、懷讓問：如何是祖師西來意？師云：何不問自己意？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Combined Essentials of the Lamps (聯燈會要), National Teacher Huian section: Tanran and Nanyue Huairang jointly ask the west-coming question; Huian answers. The singular MasterName field is therefore null and both the joint utterance and named context are explicit.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: 有僧坦然、懷讓問 names two monks jointly as utterers of the one question, so no singular MasterName can represent the turn.

Occurrences.Kwic: 趙州行脚時參師，遇師洗脚次，州便問：如何是祖師西來意？師云：恰值老僧洗脚。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Tiansheng Expanded Lamp Record (天聖廣燈錄), Linji Yixuan section. Zhaozhou Congshen is the exact questioner who asks for the meaning of the patriarch's coming from the west while Linji washes his feet; Linji Yixuan gives the following answer.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問：如何是祖師西來意？師云：西來無意。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Combined Essentials of the Lamps (聯燈會要), in Damei Fachang's record. An unnamed monk is the exact speaker of the headword question; Damei answers, ‘there was no intention in coming from the West’ (西來無意). The line, expanded context, section header, book title, TEI header, and parallel passage do not name the questioning monk.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問。如何是祖師西來意。師曰。汝問不當。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), section on Jingshan Daoqin: an unnamed monk asks the exact headword question, and Jingshan answers that the question is improper. The line, expanded context, section header, book title, TEI header, and parallel passage do not name the questioning monk.

Occurrences.Kwic: 洪州泐潭法會禪師問馬祖。如何是祖師西來意。祖曰。低聲。近前來。向汝道。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元). Letan Fahui is explicitly named as the exact questioner who asks Mazu Daoyi, 'What is the ancestral teacher's meaning in coming from the west?' Mazu tells him to lower his voice and come closer, then strikes him.

Occurrences.Kwic: 五祖云。頻呼小玉元無事只要檀郎認得聲。如何是祖師西來意。庭前柏樹子。如何是佛麻三斤。圓悟遂長噓一聲忽然有悟。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Continued Record of the Lamp (續傳燈錄), Lingyin Huiyuan's report to Emperor Xiaozong: Lingyin recounts Wuzu Fayan placing the west-coming question with Zhaozhou Congshen's cypress answer beside the Buddha question with Dongshan Shouchu's three-catties-of-hemp answer, immediately before Yuanwu Keqin's awakening.
